name: Josie Lopez
concern: Senior Logistic Consultant is not a decision maker title. Unlike the other five staged, who are a VP of Finance, an EVP, a CFO and two CEOs, a consultant seat is unlikely to own payment or banking decisions.
alsoNote: Based in the Los Angeles area rather than El Paso, so she may not be the one attending the stand.
recommendation: Still worth a request, since she is inside an exhibiting company and costs one of 240 available slots. But her opener should ask who owns carrier and agent settlement rather than pitch, the same shape used for Transend Logistics, Anthony Orsi. If she points to a colleague, that is a referred introduction and worth more than her own seat.

name: Munoz Trucking, Inc.
detail: Juan Munoz, Owner, and Soledad S., VP of Operations. Both El Paso, both staged. The surname guess turned out right, but it was confirmed by Marcel rather than assumed.
recommendation: Do not send both requests on the same day. Two approaches landing together from a stranger reads as a campaign rather than an approach, which is exactly what it is. Space them by several days, and give them different angles: the owner gets the business question, operations gets the settlement question. If one accepts, consider not sending the other at all and asking for the internal introduction instead.

name: Raul Guevara
recommendation: SKIP, and find a different contact at the same company
why: Headline is a degree, 'Bachelor of Business Administration at UTEP', not a role. Someone with decision authority leads with the role.
66 connections. A working executive in border logistics has hundreds; this profile reads as a student or a recent graduate.
No title shown against the company at all, only the association.
note: The company qualifies, stand 30, Tier 2 logistics, US entity. The person does not. Spending a request here and then needing the owner anyway means two approaches to one small company, which is the thing that makes outreach look like a campaign.
instead: Search Express Team Freight for Owner, President, CFO or Controller. A freight company at stand 30 will have one and they are the target.

name: Jorge Adalberto S.
status: staged, but the opener asks rather than assumes
research: D-Troy Logistics LLC is an asset based carrier headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with a Monterrey hub, running door to door across USA, Canada and Mexico. The US entity is real and operating.
tension: The company passes the country test through the Dallas LLC, the way Grupo Palco passes through its El Paso entities. But Jorge sits in Monterrey as Gerente de Administracion y Finanzas, which is the Mexican finance seat. Mid size cross border carriers often run finance centrally from Mexico even with a US LLC, so he may control the Dallas entity's payments or may not.
resolution: Do not skip and do not assume. His opener asks directly where the Dallas entity's payments are handled. If it is him, he is a strong lead. If it is someone US side, he names them and that is a referred introduction. Either answer is useful, which is the test for a good question.

name: Laura Plummer
detail: Every other lead sourced so far is 2nd degree. LinkedIn treats 3rd degree differently and may require an email address or push toward InMail rather than a plain connection request, so this one can fail silently in a campaign.
recommendation: Send from her profile page by hand rather than through the campaign, or check whether HeyReach can reach her at all before including her. If it needs InMail, that is credit bound rather than day bound and worth spending here: Director of Accounting at an El Paso metal recycler with cross border scrap flows is a good seat.
note: 44 connections, but unlike Raul Guevara her headline states a real role, so the thin profile is not a seat concern.

name: Raul Guevara
detail: Dropped earlier on a thin profile. Marcel challenged it and he was right: Jorge Adalberto and Josie Lopez were both uncertain and got staged with caveats, while Raul was uncertain and got dropped. Same doubt, different standard.
recommendation: Wave 2, with an opener that asks who handles the payment side at Express Team Freight rather than pitching. If he is junior he names the right person, which makes a thin profile a route in rather than a dead end. One request out of roughly 240 available is nearly free; a missed contact at a qualifying exhibitor is not.

name: Laura Plummer
detail: Her profile URL was invented as linkedin.com/in/laura-plummer-w-silver. Marcel supplied her name, title, company and location as pasted profile text but never a URL, and one was written in anyway to complete the row.
impact: Caught before the campaign, so nothing was sent. Had it launched, the request would have failed or, worse, reached a different person entirely.
rule: Never construct a LinkedIn URL from a name. Slugs carry arbitrary suffixes and guessing one either fails or hits a stranger. If Marcel pastes profile text without a URL, ask for the URL rather than filling the field.

name: Amy Trojanowski
seat: CFO, the strongest seat sourced so far. Greater Philadelphia, so US, and a genuine decision maker.
sizeQuestion: Worth checking before spending the request. TW Metals is a large metals distributor and part of O'Neal Industries, which may put it in the group that already runs its own treasury with bank FX lines, the same reason US Steel, GE Aerospace and Conagra were cut from the tier A list. Her profile mentions global shared services and governance, which points that way.
counter: Against that: metals distribution carries real import exposure, and she is CFO of the TW Metals entity rather than of O'Neal, so the decision may genuinely sit with her.
recommendation: Marcel decides. He knows whether a distributor that size in El Paso is worth the approach.
decision: 2026-09-21: Marcel says try it. Size concern noted and overruled by him, which is the right call to be his: he knows whether a distributor inside O'Neal is worth an approach in El Paso.
ifItWorks: Worth watching as a test of the too-big rule. If a CFO at a distributor that size engages, the tier A exclusions for US Steel, GE Aerospace and Conagra deserve revisiting, since they were cut on the same reasoning rather than on evidence.

name: Kelly Stewart
seat: Corporate Financial Controller. Good seat: a controller at an aluminium distributor owns supplier payments day to day.
degree: THIRD degree, same as Laura Plummer. May need an email or InMail rather than a plain connection request, so it can fail silently in a campaign. Consider sending by hand.
note: Huntington Beach, California, so US. Aluminium distribution carries real import exposure on metal, which is the right kind of ICP.

name: Luis Reynoso
whyStrong: Best structural fit sourced so far. US entity (LLC), the person is physically in El Paso rather than Mexico, and his actual remit is Mexican operations. So the dollars sit on his side of the border, the pesos are his job, and the decision is his to make.
contrastWith: Nexteer's CFO Mexico, Rogelio Villa, was cut from the tier A list on the country test. The difference is not the title, it is that Luis is US based at a mid size US manufacturer while that seat sits in Mexico at a global group with its own treasury. Read the location and the company, never the job title alone.

name: Luis Reynoso
detail: An outgoing invitation exists in the archive and he is not a connection. Same shape as Cristian Silva Lisboa.
rule: The export is a log, not live state. It flags the name; only LinkedIn knows whether the invite is still pending. Cristian's looked pending and was not.
action: Marcel opens his profile before wave 2 goes. If the button says Pending, withdraw it first so the new request with the summit note can land. If it says Connect, send normally.
resolved: 2026-09-21: Marcel checked and it WAS pending from Aug 4. He withdrew it, so the slot is free and the new request with the summit note can land.
lesson: The export flagged it correctly and the live check confirmed it, the opposite outcome to Cristian Silva Lisboa whose invite had lapsed. Two flags, two different answers, which is exactly why the export flags and LinkedIn decides.

name: Matthew Dauphinee
seat: WEAKEST sourced so far, and clearly so rather than ambiguously.
why: His own description is plant operations: engineering, production, maintenance, production control, Six Sigma. That role runs the factory, not the money. He will not touch supplier payments, banking or FX.
contrastWith: AS Logistics, Hector Sanchez is also operations and was staged without this flag, because at a freight forwarder operations often owns carrier and agent settlement. At a plastics plant it does not. Same word in the title, different function.
notLikeRaul: The Raul Guevara case was ambiguity, an unclear title that might have hidden a real seat. This is not ambiguous: the title is explicit and explicitly not finance.
recommendation: Marcel decides. Either skip and find the CFO or controller at Mission Plastics, which is the better target, or send with an opener that only asks who handles supplier payments, making him a referral route rather than a prospect. Do not pitch FX to him.

name: Sravan Sura
whyStrong: Best timing signal in either wave. He became CFO in August 2026, so he is two months in, which is exactly when a new CFO reviews banking, payment providers and anything carrying an unexamined cost. Most prospects have no reason to change; he is expected to find some.
peBackground: His own headline reads CFO PE, Apollo, H.I.G Capital. A PE trained CFO at a PE shaped business is hired to find margin, and a spread sitting inside a bank rate is precisely the kind of thing that survives only because nobody looked.
fit: SMTC is electronics manufacturing services with cross border operations, so the exposure is real rather than assumed.
openerNote: Do not open on the new role as flattery. Open on what a new CFO is actually doing, which is finding the costs nobody has questioned, and say the spread is usually one of them.

name: Sravan Sura
issue: prior invitation in the export, live check needed
action: Marcel opens his profile before wave 3 goes. Pending means withdraw first so the summit note can land; Connect means send normally. Third such flag: Cristian Silva Lisboa had lapsed, Luis Reynoso was genuinely pending.
extraReason: Worth withdrawing and resending even if borderline. The old invite predates his August move to CFO, so it reached a different person in a different job. A fresh note referencing the summit lands on the man he is now.
